title: Logical backup: what it is good for and where it stops being enough

videos.script: pg_dump does not copy the database's files. It connects like any client, reads everything, and writes down how to build it again. {{dump}} That one fact explains this whole lesson. A dump can move between versions and machines, because it is only instructions. {{formats}} It is also blind to anything outside the database it reads. In this lesson you restore the shop into a brand new server. The rows arrive, and four errors arrive with them. {{errors}} The roles that own the tables were never in the dump. They live in the server, beside every database, and they need a file of their own. {{globals}} Next comes the everyday case, a DELETE with the wrong WHERE. You bring back one table, from the dump, without touching anything else. {{partial}} Last, you make the shop sixty times bigger, and time the restore. {{timing}} That number, multiplied out, is where a logical backup stops being enough.
